evidence.note: An opaque white Insight card with a soft shadow floats bottom-right; the timeline and swarm diagram behind it are blurred and faded, but their shapes (fan of agent lines, red/black dots, Package mirror and Automated scorer boxes) stay recognisable.
The 'A universal cheat' card sits sharp with a shadow, while the diagram to its right is clearly blurred yet still readable as the swarm fanning into the package mirror.
Two shadowed cards cover most of the diagram; the slivers left visible are blurred, so the context is mostly hidden but the cards clearly hold focus.
The wide 'A research programme' card hides almost all of the diagram; only the blurred legend shows beneath it. The focus is clear, but little context is visible at this step.
The quote cards sit beside the diagram, not over it, and soft shadows lift them off the page without fighting the diagram.
The title stays sharp above the blur at every overlay step, so the slide keeps its anchor.

rationale: At the insight step and the first pop-over step, blur plus shadow make the overlay clearly the focus while the diagram beneath is softened but still identifiable, which matches the pass anchor. At steps 3–4 the opaque cards hide much of the diagram, which weakens how much context shows, but the little that shows is still blurred and recognisable, and the overlay never tangles with the content. Overall the depth effects separate focus from context as the style intends.
